basis: Osteopetrosis with antibody deficiency; visual loss 8/8; marrow compromise is common in malignant osteopetrosis. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish organ damage.
Predominantly CNS tumor; retinal capillary tumors annotated in 80-99%. Neurogenic bladder and bowel symptoms do not establish direct urinary or intestinal disease.
Ossification directly affects the cartilage of the external ear.
Lysosomal sphingolipid degradation disorders; neurologic and visceral damage vary substantially by subtype and are not established in most patients across this umbrella.
Defining hypoparathyroidism, hypocalcemia and skeletal dysplasia. Hypocalcemic seizures do not establish intrinsic brain damage; dental caries is a separate disease.
Complex spastic paraplegia; kyphosis 9/9, joint hypermobility 8/8 and pectus deformity 7/9 establish skeletal involvement. Hypertrichosis alone is not skin damage.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome with intellectual disability in 19/24; strabismus 26/48 and hearing impairment 13/24 support ocular and ear dysfunction.
Skeletal dysplasia, retinal degeneration and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; sensorineural hearing loss is also a defining diagnostic feature.
Primary respiratory ciliopathy; recurrent otitis 3/4 and structural heart defects, several each affecting 2/6, support ear and cardiac involvement. Situs changes alone are not damage.
Hereditary episodic cerebellar dysfunction. Weakness and abnormal eye movements are neurologic manifestations, without established intrinsic muscle or eye disease.
Telomere disorder with marrow and skin/nail disease; pulmonary fibrosis 3/6 and hepatic fibrosis 2/6. Oral leukoplakia and osteoporosis (3/6) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: skin is the tumor site, lymphocytes are the malignant cells, and lymphoma requires the infectious_immune axis.
Opportunistic fungal infection with heterogeneous cutaneous, pulmonary and disseminated presentations; the definition does not establish any particular organ in most patients.
Congenital branchial-remnant cyst or fistula occupying lateral cervical soft tissue/subcutis. Pharyngeal embryologic origin alone does not establish airway damage.
Defined as a CNS disorder causing ataxia, dysarthria and incoordination; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic ocular damage.
Cobalamin remethylation defect with megaloblastic anemia; developmental delay 2/2 and brain atrophy in 30-79%. Specific damaging eye findings and thrombosis are occasional.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia from defective cartilage sulfation; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and causes severe respiratory failure.
Primary antibody deficiency. Respiratory infections and associated autoimmune diseases are separate conditions; lasting organ damage is not present in most patients.
Inherited structural cardiomyopathy affecting left ventricular myocardial compaction.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast is outside the thirteen axes. Stromal fibrosis does not change its organ of origin.
Variable mosaic malformation syndrome with CNS/developmental and skeletal abnormalities; all individual supplied findings are occasional (5-29%), supporting no additional axes.
Malignant tumor arising in a cranial nerve. Particular ocular or auditory sites occur in subtypes and do not apply across the umbrella.
Carcinoma arising in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the thirteen axes; squamous histology alone does not establish a separate skin origin.
Congenital urinary tract dysfunction involving reflux between bladder and ureters; associated renal hypoplasia remains within the renal axis.
Immune dysregulation with dermatitis in 15/16; airway disease/asthma in 11/16 and gastrointestinal eosinophilic infiltration in 10/16 establish common organ involvement.
